label: input token 3 during copy phase (and weakly at t=0)
explanation: Token-detector for the digit 3 as input. Fires on every copy-phase step whose fed-back input is 3 (strong, ~0.6-0.99; about 96% of activation mass), and weakly (~0.17) when 3 is the first original token at t=0. Does not fire on 3 at later original-phase positions (t>=1, near zero), on the delimiter, or on any other token. Magnitude is highest right after <DEL> (3 as the first copied token) and is largely independent of L, recall position, or output token.

issues: Minor: 3 at t=1 is not completely silent. It fires weakly on about 10% of occurrences (precision 0.098 for in_tok==3 & t==1, 0.3% of mass). 'Near zero' is still a fair description, and t>=2 really is near zero (177 or fewer active steps).

The remaining misses are weak (about 0.11 to 0.14 relative) activations on non-3 tokens, mostly at the first copy steps. Together they hold 0.7% of mass on the test split, and they look like scattered noise rather than a pattern.

Claims checked: copy-phase 3 has precision 1.0. 3 at t=0 has precision 1.0 and fires weakly (all in the lowest activation quartile). The delimiter step never fires. Rate is flat across L, to_go and recall_idx. recall_idx==1 is over-represented in the top quartile (23% vs about 15% base), which supports 'top activations right after <DEL>'. The predicate has 0 false positives on test.
